inputs.original_text: Daniel Rubenstein’s talk of “success” and political resolution looks like cover for keeping the operation—and the pressure on Iran—alive. Israel’s refusal to bend on Iran’s nuclear and missile programs makes the peace language sound more like narrative management than a genuine change of course. They want the public to accept both stories at once because that contradiction keeps scrutiny away from who benefits from the operation continuing.
inputs.modified_text: Daniel Rubenstein’s talk of “success” and political resolution sounds less like a real change of course than a carefully managed story to keep the operation—and pressure on Iran—going. Israel’s refusal to bend on Iran’s nuclear and missile programs makes the peace language look like a distraction: the public is being asked to accept two contradictory narratives while attention stays off who benefits from the operation continuing.
